title: Unique identifier linking in user data store
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account data containing unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that can link data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in user data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes (email, username, etc.) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data to individuals through attribute combination.

title: Processing of identified parent account data
description: The system requests and processes identified parent account data, which directly identifies the data subject.

title: Unique identifier in user account data
description: The MongoDB users collection contains unique references to the identity of the data subject through account identifiers.

title: Quasi-identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification.

title: Attributable data evidence from stored accounts
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their account or actions.

title: Potentially sensitive parent account data types
description: Parent account data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected when strictly required for the authentication service functionality.

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Parent account data may be stored longer than functionally needed for the authentication service, creating unnecessary privacy risk.

title: Excessive party access to parent account data
description: Parent account data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators or other services.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Parent account data may be stored longer than needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for the stored parent account data.

title: JWT Token Contains Unique Identifier
description: The JWT token transmitted in this flow contains unique identifiers that can be used to link data across different systems or sessions, potentially enabling tracking of user activities.
assumptions: JWT tokens typically contain unique session/user identifiers

title: User Data Combined with JWT Creates Quasi-identifier
description: The combination of user data with JWT token information may create quasi-identifiers that can be used to link data about individuals across different contexts.
assumptions: User data contains multiple attributes that, when combined with JWT, form a quasi-identifier

title: Processing of Identified Data
description: The flow transmits identified user data along with JWT tokens, which means the system is processing data that directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: JWT and user data contain identifiable information about the parent user

title: JWT Contains Unique Reference to Identity
description: The JWT token serves as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification across systems.
assumptions: JWT tokens are designed to uniquely identify authenticated users

title: Potentially Sensitive User Data Collected
description: User data transmitted may include sensitive personal information that exceeds what is functionally required for authentication purposes.
assumptions: User data may contain more sensitive attributes than needed for the authentication service

title: Data Propagated to Parent User
description: User data is propagated to the parent user (EE1) where it may be accessible beyond the immediate authentication context.
assumptions: Parent user may have access to user data beyond authentication needs

title: Unawareness of Data Transmission
description: The data subject may not be fully aware that their user data is being transmitted to the parent user in this flow.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into all data flows involving their information

title: Lack of Control Over Data Sharing
description: The data subject may lack control over how their user data is shared with the parent user through this authentication flow.
assumptions: Users may not have granular control over data sharing preferences

title: Potential Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: The transmission of user data alongside JWT may process more personal data than is actually needed for authentication functionality.
assumptions: Authentication may not require all user data attributes to be transmitted

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Email addresses are globally unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child user through data correlation.
assumptions: Email+password combination is unique to the user

title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) during child login, directly identifying the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are personally identifiable information

title: Identifier processing
description: Parent email is a unique identifier that directly references the identity of the parent data subject, processed during child authentication.
assumptions: Email is a unique reference to parent identity

title: Revealing attributes
description: Email and password are revealing attributes that support identification of both the child user and the parent data subject.
assumptions: Login credentials reveal identity information

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for authentication functionality.
assumptions: Password is more sensitive than necessary for basic login

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Password data may be stored, logged, or processed beyond what is functionally needed for authentication, creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Password processing extends beyond authentication

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Child user may not be aware that their login transmits parent's email and password, and the implications for parent's privacy.
assumptions: Child lacks full understanding of data implications

title: Lack of preferences control
description: Child user has limited control over how parent's email and password data is processed, stored, or shared by the authentication service.
assumptions: Child cannot customize data processing preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing parent email and password for child login may violate data minimization by collecting more personal data than functionally necessary.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Child user's consent may not be valid for processing parent's personal data, as children typically lack legal capacity to consent.
assumptions: Child lacks legal capacity to provide valid consent

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected and processed beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved video to a child.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video data may be disclosed at a more fine-grained level of granularity than needed for the intended purpose of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the child user) which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified data (video content) that can be associated with the child user.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video content may include revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (child user).

title: Quasi-identifier combining in video
description: Video data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., location, time, context) that can be combined to link data to an individual.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Personal data in video can be analyzed for patterns to link data to that individual through profiling.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child user may not be fully aware about the collection, processing, or disclosure of their personal data in the video stream.

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: The child user may lack control to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed in the video stream.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (video) is processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Invalid consent for video processing
description: Personal data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from the child user or their guardian.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, IP addresses) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across different contexts.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple attributes (page views, timestamps, device info, location) that can be combined to create quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification of individuals.

title: Profiling an individual through browsing patterns
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data to build profiles of individuals, inferring preferences, interests, and behaviors that link data to specific users.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (e.g., user IDs, account identifiers) that are processed and shared with advertisers.

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data includes revealing attributes such as search queries, visited pages, and interaction patterns that support identification of the data subject.

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is propagated to third-party advertisers where it may be accessible beyond the functional needs of the AI recommendation engine.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is made accessible to a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, which may be broader than functionally necessary.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected, processed, and shared with third-party advertisers.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More browsing data is processed and shared with advertisers than is actually needed for the functional goals of the AI recommendation engine.

title: JWT contains unique identifier enabling linking
description: JWT tokens typically contain unique user identifiers (user_id, session_id, etc.) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems and contexts.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information

title: JWT contains unique reference to identity
description: JWT tokens contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (user ID, authentication claims) that can be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity information

title: Sensitive authentication data stored in localStorage
description: JWT tokens contain sensitive authentication data (access tokens, refresh tokens, user claims) that should be treated as highly sensitive and may not be functionally required to be stored in client-side localStorage.
assumptions: JWT contains sensitive authentication credentials

title: JWT retention exceeds functional necessity
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage persist until manually cleared or session expires, potentially longer than functionally needed for authentication purposes.
assumptions: JWTs are stored persistently in localStorage

title: localStorage accessible to multiple parties
description: Browser localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running in the browser, including malicious scripts, extending beyond the predetermined set of parties (authentication service).
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to third-party scripts

title: User unawareness of JWT storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, as this is typically not disclosed in privacy policies or user interfaces.
assumptions: Users are not informed about JWT storage

title: Lack of user control over JWT storage
description: Users cannot easily control or customize how JWT tokens are stored, managed, or deleted from localStorage without technical knowledge.
assumptions: Users lack technical ability to manage localStorage

title: Difficulty in rectification/erasure of JWT data
description: Users may not be able to easily delete or rectify JWT tokens stored in localStorage, as this requires browser-level access or technical intervention.
assumptions: Users lack ability to delete localStorage data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage may process more personal data than strictly necessary, as tokens contain user identity and authentication information that could be handled more securely.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific JWT content and organizational policies

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage may persist longer than functionally needed, violating storage limitation requirements under GDPR.
assumptions: GDPR storage limitation principle applies
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific JWT expiration and retention policies

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable or quasi-identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of attributes in child history (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child when combined.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes child history which is identified personal data about the child data subject.
assumptions: Child history contains personally identifiable information
